Regimes of the edges of a tree from a list of clades

Source: R/damocles_regimes.R
clade_regimes.Rd

clade_regimes() assigns each edge of tree to a regime named after the clade it lies in, for the regimes of damocles_fit() and damocles_test(): a partition of the tree defined a priori, such as families or biogeographic groups, against which partitions from methods that estimate shifts in rates of diversification can be compared.

Usage

clade_regimes(tree, clades, background = "background", stem = FALSE)

Arguments

tree

A rooted phylo tree.

clades

A named list with, for each clade, a character vector of its tips or one node number (of tree, as in tree$edge) at its base.

background

Name of the regime of the edges outside every clade.

stem

If TRUE, the stem edge of each clade belongs to it.

Value

A factor with one regime per edge of tree, in the order of tree$edge, with the regimes that occur as levels: background first, then the clades.

Details

A clade is the crown group of the most recent common ancestor of its tips: the edges below that node belong to the clade, and its stem edge too when stem = TRUE; a clade of one tip is its terminal edge. If the tips given are not monophyletic the clade covers every descendant of their common ancestor, with a warning. Clades later in the list override earlier ones, so nested clades go after the clades that hold them. Edges in no clade take the regime background.

See also

damocles_fit(), damocles_lrt().

Other dynamic null model: confint.mc_damocles_fit(), damocles_loglik(), damocles_lrt(), damocles_test(), simulate_damocles()

Examples

set.seed(4)
tr <- treeshapesim::sim_tree_shape(20)
# the clade of the first node after the root
reg <- clade_regimes(tr, list(A = ape::extract.clade(tr, ape::Ntip(tr) + 2)$tip.label))
table(reg)
#> reg
#> background          A 
#>          2         36
